successors.name: Senones
successors.text: the ager Gallicus between Ariminum and Ancona

ledger.x: c. 900 BC: the Umbri 'in inner central Italy, approximately between the middle Tiber river and the central Apennines' in the Iron Age; 'Most Umbrian cities were settled in the 9th-4th centuries BCE'; Umbria 'bordered by the Tiber and Nar rivers and included the Apennine slopes on the Adriatic'; earlier a larger area…

c. 390 BC: the Adriatic coast (Ariminum-Ancona) to the Senones, 'displacing the Umbrians'; undated on both pages. Split with the picentes dossier agreed 2026-10-19: the Picentes page also says 'In 390 BC, the Senoni Gauls... occupied Picenum north of the Esino river', which would make the Pesaro-Ancona strip Picene…
310-295 BC: 'The Romans first made contact with Umbria in 310 BC'; Nequinum captured 299; Sentinum 295 against 'Samnites, Gauls, Etruscans, and Umbrians'.
299 BC: 'When the Romans captured Nequinum in 299 BC'.

c. 260 BC: 'They had completed their conquest of Umbria by approximately 260 BC' (Latin colonies 299, 268, 241); the Umbrian cities stay on their land as allies of Rome, tinted from roman-republic (vassal_start umbri 260).
90 BC: 'The Umbri played a minor role in the Social War and as a result were granted citizenship in 90 BC'; the allied cities become Roman citizen communities.
90 BC: citizenship; the Umbrian communities are Roman municipalities and no separate Umbrian polity remains.

certainty.note: Umbria between the Tiber, the Nar and the Adriatic slopes; no surveyed border.
